blocks.text: LEARNING STRATEGY / CAPABILITY ARCHITECTURE
One core. Many ways to put it to work.
Several learning efforts were already underway. The harder question was how to make them work as one system.
What should be shared across the group, and what should each specialty make its own?

A groupwide learning program, new-hire development, entry resources, and specialist development paths were all in motion. The group needed common expectations, behavior standards, and a measurement approach while each capability developed its own practice.

I led the learning architecture: defining the common core and behavior-first approach, then connecting pathways, practice, resources, and measurement into one operating model. I collaborated with leadership to develop and execute this strategy.
Start with what people do. Then build the system around it.
I defined the skills and behaviors people needed to build, then identified how each team would apply them. Observable behaviors guided the architecture, with practice and support connected to work.

Shared: identity, expectations, behavior standards, and a measurement approach. Specialized: each team's practice, pathways, and leader-owned success measures. Learning journeys, the resource hub, and contribution and reuse connect the operating system.
The practice is the point.

AI-native workflows ask people to create a workspace for each new project and ship more code, designs, or experiences. We provided a prompt library, discovery-meeting coaching, and an AI tool selection guide alongside preflight checks.
Run the check: The designer runs a preflight on the design.
Review against standards: The workflow grades the design against standards, concepts, frameworks, and similar criteria.
Choose remediation: The designer receives a report and decides how to remediate.
Share review evidence: Managers and leaders were asked to request the scorecard when designers deliver work.
This example shows where support lives in the system. We are not claiming that the prompt improved call quality without an evaluation of that outcome.
Measure the system. Then ask what changed.

Team leaders help validate the framework and own success measures. The current signals tell us about use and contribution. The longer-term test is whether this work improves performance and business outcomes.
Adoption / Current signal
AI tool usage.
Contribution / Current signals
Pull requests, code changes proposed for review, and resource-hub artifacts.
Design review / Individual scorecards
Preflight results go to designers; no improvement trend is reported here.
Business outcomes / Intended
Results not yet supplied.
These counts alone do not establish behavior quality or a business result.
Specific values and outcome results are not included here. This case shows the operating architecture and the measurement approach, with those evidence limits made explicit.
